headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: ctx observes Claude Code events and can act on shared files/APIs, while awesome-prompts is an unverified prompt source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt-content source, and ctx explicitly observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events via MCP hooks. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if ctx ingests prompt text or files from the same workspace. The pair lacks direct evidence of a shared channel, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF ctx ingests files or prompt text originating from awesome-prompts, injection becomes actionable.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP channel, attacker-controlled prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of prompt files by ctx.
Place awesome-prompts content in a read-only directory.
Add provenance tags before ctx consumes any prompt artifact.
Review MCP hook inputs for instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or allowlist parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content, while awesome-prompts is a content-writing repository with no declared data classes. Because ctx can call APIs and read files, a shared workspace could leak local artifacts into external services; however, the pair does not show sensitive data in agent_a, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts is placed in the same workspace as ctx logs or graph data, ctx may ingest and transmit those files.
IF ctx forwards file contents to GitHub, Claude Code, or other APIs, workspace data can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep ctx and awesome-prompts in separate directories.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running ctx.
Restrict ctx API credentials to non-sensitive repos.
Inspect runtime logs for file-content capture.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and run multiple instances, while awesome-prompts is a repository-like content source that may also be edited locally. Overlapping write access to the same directory can cause clobbering or inconsistent state, but there is no evidence of unrestricted concurrent git mutation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF ctx runs multiple instances against one workspace, concurrent edits can race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Run only one ctx instance per workspace.
Back up the repository before edits.
requires-engineering: add transactional write coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes tool events and manages context, so it can treat upstream content as operational input; awesome-prompts supplies prompt material that may be reused as authoritative guidance. If ctx acts on that content without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or corrupted context. The interaction is plausible in default setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ctx uses awesome-prompts content as authoritative instructions, unverified errors can propagate.
IF ctx triggers API calls or file actions based on that content, downstream mistakes become persistent.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on imported prompts.
Mark imported content as untrusted in ctx.
Compare outputs against a second source.
Limit ctx to read-only observation for the first run.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data class is declared for awesome-prompts, while ctx does touch logs and graph data but no specific regulated class is identified. The pair therefore shows only a generic compliance gap around logging/retention, not a documented residency or certification mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into ctx logs or graph data, retention and residency controls must be rechecked.
IF awesome-prompts is repurposed to store sensitive prompts, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace.
Review log retention settings before first run.
Document data classes allowed in ctx.
Separate personal and project repositories.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive data classes.
